scope: China/Jiangsu/Xuzhou public evidence; P0 accessibility-first field selection
purpose: Broaden the search for easy-to-reach potential gradients while subtracting exchange structures that are already organized by markets, communities, platforms or public programs.

evidence: Xuzhou youth-night-school partner model already uses small shops and other local spaces to host learning/activity demand.
Xuzhou communities are already converting underused kindergarten rooms, property rooms and other public/community spaces into active resident service space.
Jiangsu complete-community programs explicitly build resource inventories and share community facilities across nearby neighborhoods.
observed_market_closure.reopen_only_if: a specific private time-slot remains repeatedly idle, has a named controller willing to activate it on non-rent economics, and a repeated nearby outcome is not served by youth-night-school, community or commercial venue routes

evidence: Xuzhou OPC communities already hold business-matching events and have helped student/young founders sign enterprise orders.
Jiangsu universities already use external mentors and reveal-list mechanisms to connect students with enterprise pain points.
Xuzhou 2026 OPC training has already trained hundreds of students and aims to cover more than one thousand students across local universities.
observed_market_closure.reopen_only_if: a recurring task class is below agency and institutional matching thresholds, has objective acceptance, and is paid rather than disguised free student labor

evidence: Jiangsu is explicitly expanding shared parking across public institutions, commercial facilities, office buildings, sports venues, schools and communities.
The province is integrating parking into a unified public parking database with reservation and digital payment support.
Jiangsu communities are already converting idle public space into elderly meal points and market-operated community canteens.
Existing models include central kitchens, community meal points, delivery, public-space provision and commercial operator investment.

actors: experienced retirees / senior professionals with industry judgment, credibility, relationships or commercial context
young OPC / AI founders with strong technical execution but weak brand, customer proof, channel access and negotiation context
narrowed_first_wave.observed_gradient: one side retains industry trust, judgment and relationship capital after leaving full-time organizational roles; the other side has new AI/technical execution but weak commercial legitimacy and customer access
public_support: Xuzhou reporting in August 2026 says OPC founders commonly have technology but lack brand recognition, customer cases, channel resources and business experience.
Jiangsu has more than 12,000 people in silver-talent pools and already uses retired experts for enterprise support, industry mentoring and youth development.
Existing OPC programs already provide general mentors and occasional business matching, which is counterevidence against generic mentoring.
narrowed_first_wave.missing_edge_question: After subtracting mentoring and public expert-service programs, is there a recurring lightweight commercial role in which a senior person contributes bounded customer-context, trust transfer, qualification, negotiation preparation or channel navigation to one specific OPC outcome without returning to employment or becoming a full consultant?
why_easy_to_enter: both actor classes can be approached through public communities, universities, retiree/industry networks or ordinary personal introductions
the first probe requires no proprietary enterprise dataset, procurement process, software build or large capital
the hypothesis can be falsified with separate actor interviews before anyone is paired
narrowed_first_wave.first_decisive_probe: Interview 5 senior transition actors and 5 young OPC founders separately. On the senior side capture what judgment/trust/channel assets remain callable, what they refuse to do, and acceptable commitment shape. On the OPC side capture the most recent lost/blocked customer outcome, why current mentors/community matching did not solve it, and whether a bounded senior contribution would materially change that outcome.
narrowed_first_wave.promotion_gate: at least 3/5 OPC actors report the same bounded commercial blockage after existing supports; at least 3/5 senior actors possess relevant callable assets and prefer a non-employment bounded role; at least 2 pair-types can define an objective outcome and economic/reciprocal commitment
kill_conditions: OPC communities or existing mentors already solve the same blockage adequately
senior contribution is only generic advice
the value depends on opaque personal influence or improper relationship use
the role requires permanent employment or recurring founder delivery
no actor will make a real commitment

actors: caregivers / parents returning from a care-related career interruption who retain professional or management capability but have fragmented schedules
OPC, microbusinesses or small organizations that need bounded professional outcomes but cannot justify a full-time hire
narrowed_first_wave.observed_gradient: professional capability can remain after care responsibilities destroy contiguous work-time; small organizations can have real accounting, research, customer, QA, design, operations or administrative outcomes that are too small for a full-time role
public_support: current flexible-employment policy strongly expands 'mom jobs' and home-near employment.
published legal/employment analysis notes that many 'mom jobs' remain concentrated in labor-intensive or service work and that some highly educated mothers cannot find professional-role matches.
policy already encourages professional and management positions to be made flexible, proving the capability pool is not limited to low-skill work.
narrowed_first_wave.missing_edge_question: Is there a repeatable class of higher-value, outcome-bounded professional work that fits fragmented recurring time better than ordinary employment or gig platforms, while giving small organizations a capability they would otherwise leave undone?
why_easy_to_enter: no sensitive enterprise data is needed to establish the underlying schedule/capability mismatch
actors are reachable through ordinary community, professional and small-business channels
first truth can be learned from role history, available time shape, recent missed outcomes and existing workaround rather than from personal vulnerability profiling
narrowed_first_wave.first_decisive_probe: Interview 8 care-transition professionals with prior verifiable skills and 8 small operators. Do not ask about intimate family circumstances; capture skill evidence, usable time pattern, tasks they can own to acceptance, recent small-operator outcomes left undone, present alternatives and willingness to contract for a bounded result.
narrowed_first_wave.promotion_gate: at least 4 skilled actors show verifiable professional capability plus a stable fragmented-time pattern; at least 4 small operators show recurring outcome classes that do not justify a full-time hire; at least 2 outcome classes have objective acceptance and a lawful paid contract shape
kill_conditions: available work collapses to low-value piecework already served by current platforms
tasks require real-time continuous presence incompatible with the time pattern
the model relies on underpaying caregivers because of constrained availability
no payer makes a real commitment

narrowed_first_wave.decision: use it as a parent formation that can emit narrower exchanges such as PF-OPC-SILVER-CHANNEL-COPILOT-007; do not build a retiree/student marketplace

second_wave.gradient: resident skills and trusted local attention may exist while volunteer-only and full-commercial service are both the wrong commitment level
second_wave.counterevidence: Xuzhou and other Jiangsu communities already use resident hosts, volunteers, small-shop partners and shared spaces extensively
second_wave.next_truth: observe whether a repeated service/outcome remains unserved specifically because its commitment level sits between volunteering and a normal commercial service

second_wave.gradient: recent graduates may have new AI/digital capability but weak proof of work and customer trust; small actors may have bounded outcomes below full hiring thresholds
second_wave.counterevidence: Xuzhou has large public employment programs, OPC training, internships and enterprise matching; generic graduate-job or student-project matching is already heavily organized
second_wave.next_truth: only reopen around a paid proof-producing task class that existing employment, internship and OPC routes systematically do not serve

current_decision.next_blocker: actor-side direct truth from separate opt-in conversations; no pairing and no product pitch before repeated gradients are observed
